perf.summary: Drop the unused velocity arrays/pointers from the per-constraint solve call: they are dead loads and dead arguments.
perf.currentCost: Each loop iteration computes two extra pointer addresses (&velocities[idxA], &velocities[idxB]) and pushes the velocities base pointer plus two pointer args into DistanceConstraint.Solve, which never reads *velA/*velB. That is 2 extra LEA/address computations and 3 extra argument moves per constraint, plus a dependency on idxA/idxB before the call even though the velocities are irrelevant.
perf.proposedChange: Remove the velocities parameter from SolveDistanceConstraints (and velA/velB from DistanceConstraint.Solve), so the loop only forms &positions[idxA]/&positions[idxB]. Since Solve is AggressiveInlining the compiler MAY eliminate the dead args after inlining, but trimming the signature guarantees it and shrinks the public API to only what is used.
perf.rationale: Eliminates redundant address arithmetic and argument register/stack traffic in the hottest loop of the solver. Fewer live values reduces register pressure inside the (large constraintCount) loop and shortens the dependency chain to the actual position update.
perf.risk: Signature change is API-breaking; callers passing velocities must be updated. Observable position output is unchanged because velA/velB are provably unused in Solve. If the velocity arrays are intended for a future velocity-projection step, keep them but still drop the per-iteration &velocities indexing until used.

perf.summary: Hoist the dt*dt reciprocal out of the per-constraint loop and pass it to Solve as a precomputed invDtSq.
perf.currentCost: Inside DistanceConstraint.Solve, alpha = compliance / (dt*dt) recomputes dt*dt and a divide for every constraint, even though dt is constant for the whole SolveDistanceConstraints call. That is one mul + one divide per constraint that depends only on a loop-invariant.
perf.proposedChange: Compute float invDtSq = 1.0f / (dt * dt); once before the loop in SolveDistanceConstraints (guarding dt below threshold once), and pass invDtSq into a Solve overload that does alpha = compliance * invDtSq. This turns a per-constraint divide into a per-constraint multiply.
perf.rationale: Strength-reduces a per-iteration division to a multiplication and removes a redundant invariant computation from the hot loop, lowering throughput cost across constraintCount iterations.
perf.risk: Changes Solve's signature/overload. Numerically compliance*(1/(dt*dt)) is not always bit-identical to compliance/(dt*dt) due to rounding of the reciprocal; for an iterative solver this is negligible but not bit-exact. If dt can be ~0, the single hoisted reciprocal must reproduce the existing per-call behavior (currently Solve would produce inf alpha and then return via the w+alpha guard only if alpha is finite); verify the dt<1e-8 path is handled at the caller as it is in UpdateVelocity.
